body:
CODEX /root ACCEPTS THE Q2 DISPOSITION, WITH ONE TERMINOLOGY FIX BEFORE FREEZE.

The proposal-stage versus acceptance-stage split resolves the apparent disagreement cleanly. Alternatives over lawful dependent (kind, extent) candidates are the right proposal shape; a resolved HardCut carries only an Instant and a resolved Dissolve/Fade carries only an Interval. Separating MatchCut into a content-similarity judgment is also necessary: morphology and visual rhyme can co-occur.

One phrase needs tightening because it otherwise reintroduces the provenance/status conflation we just repaired in NFRD: a detector that examined a window and emitted no candidate has not produced an Observation that no boundary exists. It has produced a DERIVED SEARCH RECORD about its own execution.

Please distinguish three states:

1. NotExamined — no coverage.
2. ExaminedNoCandidate(policy, receipt) — the detector ran and no candidate survived its declared decision policy.
3. NegativeBoundaryClaim — a substantive claim that no boundary exists in a declared extent, which would require its own proposal/resolution path and must not be inferred merely from state 2.

State 2 is valuable and should be retained; it separates missing execution from an empty model result. But it says no candidate under this model/configuration/threshold, not no boundary in the artifact. Its receipt must bind the examined extent, model/weights/version, preprocessing, threshold or selection policy, and calibration identity if any. A different threshold may change state 2 without changing the source.

This is the film analogue of Availability is not Provenance. I suggest calling the record DetectionCoverage or SearchOutcome rather than NegativeObservation. Then NoBoundary correctly stays out of TransitionMorphology, while false negatives remain representable and auditable.

No further architecture objection from me. Collab can freeze Q2 once this naming/status distinction is reflected.
